newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Bids softer, supply sells - Sept 4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Bids softer, supply sells - Sept 4.

text.p: New municipal bond supply was soaked up at "fair" market levels on Wednesday, while secondary prices fell 1/4 point in thin trade, dealers said.

Despite the drop, secondary prices were mostly higher than lows seen on Tuesday, when bids fell as much as five to 10 basis points before rebounding. Traders said inventories were still light enough to underpin the bid side.
"On a relative basis the market still does not feel heavy," one trader said. "It's quiet but there is a bid."

Weakness on Wednesday reflected Treasury volatility ahead of the much anticipated August payrolls report on Friday, traders said. Treasuries sold off in a consolidation of Tuesday's gains, analysts said, with market players looking to sell any upticks.
Treasuries posted muted reaction when the Commerce Department said construction spending fell 1.4 percent in July to its lowest rate since February.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 14/32 to yield 7.10 percent at 1624 EDT.

Tax-exempt bids held unchanged in early trade, with some trades posting gains from a softer Tuesday session, traders said. A block of Intermountain Power Agency 5.95 percent revenue bonds due 2017 traded at 5.95 percent less 1/4 point compared with an early bid of 6.00 percent less 1/8 point.
New issues garnered solid demand from institutional buyers, according to dealers, leaving a full plate of competitive issues with low balances by the close.
One trader forecast increased selling by institutions as the fall new issue calendar builds.
Topping the new issue slate, Morgan Stanley & Co reported a $36.9 million unsold balance from $185 million Illinois general obligation bonds with a true interest cost bid of 5.722 percent.
The scale of reofferings was in-line with market levels, said one municipal analyst.
A 5.714 percent TIC bid from Merrill Lynch & Co was rejected because the firm failed to comply with new state requirements that mandate a scale of ascending coupons.
Morgan Stanley reoffered serial bonds to yield from 4.25 percent in 1998 to 5.95 percent in 2016.
A 2018 term, containing $14.8 million, was reoffered to yield 5.97 percent and a 2021 term, containing $22.2 million, was not formally reoffered.
The entire issue is FGIC-insured and rated AAA by Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investors Service.
In other competitive action:
Goldman Sachs & Co reported a $6.1 million unsold balance from $55 million Tennessee Housing Development Agency AMT and non-AMT revenue bonds, reoffered at a top yield of 6.375 percent in 2022.
Goldman Sachs said it had a $940,000 unsold balance from $65 million Alabama Housing Finance Authority AMT and non-AMT bonds, reoffered with a top yield of 6.375 percent in 2026.
In light negotiated action, Merrill Lynch & Co priced and repriced $75 million New York State Mortgage Finance Agency AMT and non-AMT revenue bonds.
Bonds were priced with a top yield 6.40 percent in 2027.
Looking ahead, J.P. Morgan Securities said it will price $167 million Piedmont, South Carolina, MPA bonds on Thursday.
Thursday's competitive sales include $30.55 million Austin, Texas, Public Improvement bonds and $11.755 million Austin, Texas, general obligation bonds at 1200 EDT.
